text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mubarak says in meeting on European trade partnership that Egyptian economy can interact with world markets. Government will work to remove limits on agricultural exports.
- Mubarak meets U.S. senator who says his country is still committed to its promises to keep peace alive.
- Egyptian-Syrian committee begins meeting with aim of setting up free trade area and protecting joint investments.
- State employees to receive 10 percent raise in July.

- Israeli sources say doubt Mubarak-Netanyahu summit still on because of Egypt's insistence that settlements be stopped. New talks for Osama el-Baz in Israel aimed at ensuring success of summit. Foreign Minister Moussa says Sharm el-Sheikh talks are aimed at boosting Palestinian track of peace process.
- Message from Libya's Gaddafi to Mubarak on bilateral relations and Arab affairs.
- For the sake of fulfilling needs of low-income groups, Housing Ministry's new plan aims at giving 750 million pounds in loans to build houses for poor.
- Interior Ministry senior official says police successfully averted terrorist plot, will announce details soon.

- Prime Minister Ganzouri says after meeting IMF officials that Egypt, with Mubarak's leadership, continues to implement economic reform programme. Public Enterprise Minister Atef Ebeid says IMF report affirms strength of Egypt's economy.
- Netanyahu says Egypt can do a lot because it is a leading Arab country. An Israeli document says continued building of settlements will lead to war.
- Health Ministry to receive moving clinics today.
